hooks.text: Early spacewalking was so exhausting it nearly killed astronauts.
How did an astronaut conquer deadly spacewalk exhaustion?
Spacewalks were nearly impossible until astronauts practiced underwater.

title: How Gemini 12 Solved Spacewalk Exhaustion
description: Discover how Buzz Aldrin conquered deadly space fatigue on Gemini 12 by using underwater pool training.

beats.text: Early spacewalking was so exhausting it nearly killed astronauts.

beats.text: Pilots suffered extreme overheating without proper foot and body restraints.

beats.text: NASA launched Gemini 12 in November 1966 to solve the problem.

beats.text: Command pilot James Lovell and pilot Buzz Aldrin flew the mission.

beats.text: Aldrin trained for weightlessness inside an underwater neutral buoyancy pool.

beats.text: In orbit, he used custom foot restraints across three spacewalks.

beats.text: His underwater pool training definitively conquered zero-gravity physical exhaustion.

beats.text: His techniques proved human beings could safely work outside their spacecraft.
